stem: A 68-year-old client asks which routine vaccinations still matter in older adulthood. Which response best reflects current CDC guidance?

options.A: Review pneumococcal vaccination history, but omit recombinant zoster vaccine if the client has previously had shingles.
options.B: Recommend recombinant zoster vaccine, but reserve pneumococcal vaccination for adults with chronic medical conditions rather than considering age and prior doses.
options.C: Recommend recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination without reviewing prior doses because age alone determines the exact products and doses needed.
options.D: Review vaccine history and give indicated recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccines, along with other vaccines recommended by age, history, and risk factors.

rationale: Current CDC adult immunization guidance requires providers to determine vaccines by age, assess additional indications, and review vaccination history. Recombinant zoster vaccine is routinely recommended for adults age 50 years or older regardless of a prior episode of shingles or prior live zoster vaccine. Pneumococcal recommendations apply from age 50 years but the needed product or additional dose depends on prior pneumococcal vaccination history. Therefore D is correct. A incorrectly excludes RZV after prior shingles, B incorrectly makes pneumococcal vaccination dependent only on chronic disease, and C ignores the prior-dose history needed to determine the pneumococcal regimen.
educational_objective: Use the current CDC adult immunization schedule to review age, prior vaccine history, and risk factors when counseling an older adult about recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination.

source_original.stem: A 68-year-old client asks which routine vaccinations still matter in older adulthood. Which response best reflects current CDC guidance?

options.A: Review pneumococcal vaccination by age and history, but defer recombinant zoster vaccination because increasing age makes zoster vaccination inappropriate.
options.B: Recommend recombinant zoster vaccine, but omit pneumococcal vaccination unless the client has previously been hospitalized for bacterial pneumonia.
options.C: Continue influenza vaccination, but discontinue age-based zoster and pneumococcal vaccination because those vaccines are intended for younger adults.
options.D: Review vaccine history and give indicated recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccines, plus other vaccines recommended by age, history, and risk level.

source_original.rationale: Older adulthood does not end routine vaccination. The current CDC adult schedule requires review of age, prior vaccination history, and risk factors; recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccines are among the vaccines routinely considered in this age range, along with other indicated vaccines. Option D appropriately directs history-based use of the current schedule. Options A, B, and C incorrectly exclude age-indicated vaccination or impose unsupported prerequisites.
source_original.source_detail: CDC — Adult Immunization Schedule by Age, current schedule: vaccination in older adults is based on age, prior doses/history and risk factors; the ≥65-year age rows/notes include indicated recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination along with other age/risk-based vaccines. Current CDC adult schedule is the July 2, 2025 schedule as amended 2026-04-27 under the March 16, 2026 court order; current CDC schedule status live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive care, immunization, pregnancy health promotion, adherence support and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the stem, construct and key D. Replaced implausible age-exclusion distractors with realistic errors about prior shingles, chronic-disease-only pneumococcal eligibility, and failure to review prior doses. Currentness was reverified against the live CDC schedule and its 2026 court-order status notice.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC adult immunization schedule and notes
audit_findings.currentness: CDC current-status notice and live schedule rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: CDC adult notes: How to use schedule; Pneumococcal routine vaccination; Zoster routine vaccination
audit_findings.claim_audit: RZV age/history statements and pneumococcal age/history dependence are directly supported by current CDC sections; no unsupported product interval or threshold was added beyond the source.

distractor_audit.A: Prior shingles does not remove the routine RZV recommendation for adults age 50 or older.
distractor_audit.B: Pneumococcal vaccination is age-based from age 50 and is not limited to adults with chronic disease.
distractor_audit.C: Prior vaccination history is required to determine the pneumococcal regimen; age alone does not determine exact products/doses.
distractor_audit.D: Correctly directs age-, history- and risk-based review with indicated RZV and pneumococcal vaccination.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D is fully compatible with both RZV and pneumococcal schedule logic.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address the same two vaccine domains and differ by clinically meaningful schedule logic rather than absurd exclusions.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preventive care and education for adults age 65 and older.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked CDC currentness, court-order status, zoster and pneumococcal notes, all four options, rationale, objective, blueprint and second-answer risk from zero; D remained uniquely best.
